:::{#exr-bernoulli-score-contribution}
#### Score contribution of one binary outcome

In the setting of @exr-bernoulli-loglik-contribution, let:

- $\devn_\iobs \eqdef \outvar_\iobs - \prob$ be the [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean) of $\outvar_\iobs$ from its mean $\prob$;
- $\precision \eqdef 1 / \Var{\Outvar_\iobs}$ be the [precision](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-precision) of $\Outvar_\iobs$.

1.  Derive the [score](#def-score) contribution $\score_\iobs(\prob) \eqdef \deriv{\prob} \llik_\iobs(\prob)$ of observation $\iobs$.
2.  Write it using $\devn_\iobs$ and $\precision$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-score-contribution}

**1.** By definition,

$$
\score_\iobs(\prob)
= \deriv{\prob} \llik_\iobs(\prob)
$$

**2.** Using @thm-bernoulli-score,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\deriv{\prob} \llik_\iobs(\prob)
&= \precision \devn_\iobs
&& \text{(score of a Bernoulli variable, with $x = \outvar_\iobs$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The last step is @thm-bernoulli-score for the observed value $\outvar_\iobs$ of $\Outvar_\iobs$,
whose [precision](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-precision) is $\precision$ and whose [deviation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-deviation-pop-mean) is $\devn_\iobs$.

:::
